paper: arXiv:2607.13425 — Data-Efficient Adaptation of LLMs via Attention Head Reweighting (AHR), COLM 2026

findings.issue: Tweet 7's '(outside noise)' qualifier read as applying to both reproduction deltas, but only the Qwen2.5-0.5B result (-3.33, std 1.36) is outside seed noise. The GPT-2-small delta (-2.22, std 3.14) is WITHIN seed noise, so by the pre-registered variance rule it is indistinguishable from zero, not a declarable loss. Presenting it as a loss overstates the finding on the most exposed platform.

T4 juxtaposed the free two-head edit (+0.99, measured on Llama-3.2-1B over 4 datasets) against AHR's +0.53 average margin over ICL (modern-3 models, 6 datasets) as 'more than', a mismatched-basis comparison a hostile reviewer would flag: on Llama-3.2-1B itself AHR gets +3.53, so the free edit is ~28% of AHR's gain, not 'more'. It exceeds only the modern-3 AVERAGE (dragged down by 3B/8B).

Reviewer-defense drill: the strongest pro-AHR objection — since gamma merges into W_O, a trained AHR model could run demonstration-free and amortize ICL's per-query context tax into a one-time training cost — was untested by us AND by the paper, and was unaddressed in the outputs. An un-preempted objection our evidence cannot close. Acknowledged in paper Sec.3 and blog future-work; documented as objection #7 in review/objections.md. Verdict scoped to 'AHR does not beat ICL as the paper deploys it'.

findings.issue: The blog posed 'where does the advertised 6 points over LoRA on security tasks come from?' and answered with the modern-3 average AHR-LoRA over ALL SIX datasets (6.23), conflating the paper's security-specific Web/Jailbreak headline with the all-dataset average. Classic same-quantity/mismatched-basis error. Reframed to 'modern-model average across all six datasets' and added the security-vs-ICL figures (+1.2 Web, +0.3 Jailbreak).

Llama-3.2-3B AHR-ICL is exactly -0.385 (a rounding tie); outputs consistently render -0.39 while the internal predictions.json uses -0.38. Cosmetic, not an inter-output inconsistency, and it does not affect any claim (the value is negative / crosses zero between 1B and 3B either way). No change to outputs.

editor.assessment: All four platform pieces lead with the hook, keep the reproduction result prominent, and label provenance. LinkedIn stays professional and ends on an engagement question. No rewrites needed beyond the accuracy-preserving edits from passes A/B.

summary: The content suite is unusually well-grounded: every quantitative claim traces to source, the Appendix-B re-analysis independently recomputes from _appendixB.json, and a spot re-run of analyze.py regenerated summary.json bit-for-bit. Three passes found no high-severity accuracy defects — only a misapplied variance qualifier (x-thread), a mismatched-basis comparison (paper T4), and a security-vs-all-datasets conflation (blog), all fixed in place, plus one strong pro-AHR objection (AHR run demonstration-free) now acknowledged rather than dodged. Cleared to publish.
